ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.05 (Ryde voucher, NS-7) to the rider for the extra 2.16 km of the unexcused off-route segment; no account action on either party; remind the driver that a rider's "whichever way is faster" leaves the shortest-and-most-direct duty intact when the chosen route turns out longer and slower than the estimate.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the driver's 12:24 message asks about traffic, the rider's 12:25 reply is "up to you", and the complaint is a fare objection; the driver's statement is a route justification [F8][F9][F11]. Read in context, there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. SAFE-1 does not engage.

Route: the trip ran 18.0 km against a 15.1 km optimal route (+2.9 km) in 30.1 min against a 20.6 min estimate [F1][F2], and the code-settled off-route segment is 12:27–12:35, 4.90 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.75 km, adding 2.16 km [F3]. Under RD-1 any deviation not excused by RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 breaches the shortest-and-most-direct duty [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 cannot carry it: the trace marks ✗ for an incident on the replaced stretch and F14 records none [F3][F14]. The only traffic evidence is speed bands — PIE band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 12:03–12:27 and Simei Avenue band 4 during 12:03–12:49 [F12][F13] — and RD-4(b) makes a band corroborative only, insufficient to exempt a segment on its own; the PIE band window also expires as the segment begins at 12:27 [F12][F3][RD-4].

RD-3 also cannot carry it: no stop is measured in the segment and the rider named no place — her only pre-segment message is "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" [F9][F3], which is a route instruction, not a rider-named stop [RD-3].

RD-5 is the live question. F9 (12:25, before the segment start at 12:27) is a rider's general route authorisation, and F8 (12:24) shows the driver raised the congestion before leaving the optimal route, so this is not a consent_after_or_none case; F11 is an untimestamped post-trip statement and would not be consent on its own [F8][F9][F11][F3][RD-5]. A general authorisation, however, covers only a route chosen to reach the destination; it does not cover a loop that reaches nothing or a deviation of the driver's own [F9][F3][RD-5]. Here the authorisation's stated standard was speed — "whichever way is faster", "我赶时间 [I'm in a hurry]" [F9] — and the deviation produced the opposite: +2.9 km, +19% distance, and a trip 9.5 min slower than the estimate [F1][F2]. The only plausible read of F9 in context is the driver's proposal in F8, i.e. permission to take another way round the jam; the extra 2.16 km of F3 was not "a route chosen to get there" under that consent, so the segment is an unexcused detour and is refundable under RD-2.

Amount: this is a RydeTAXI meter trip, so the extra kilometres entered the fare, and the per-km rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km = $25.39 ÷ 18.01 km = $1.4098/km [F4][F7][RD-2]. Refund = 2.16 km × $1.4098/km = $3.045, rounded to $3.05 [F3][F4][RD-2]. RD-2 refunds only segment extra kilometres, so the balance of the billed excess line ($4.06 for 2.88 km) and the unattributed remainder of the +2.9 km are not refundable [F4][F1]. The $0.11 waiting line is a metered RydeTAXI waiting unit and stays [F5][F7][RD-3]; there was no surge and the other tariff lines are standard [F6][F7].

Flag: both profiles show zero upheld disputes in the last 90 days (rider 0, driver 0 over 302 trips) [F16][F17], so RD-6's repeated-breach precondition is absent and no account action attaches; profile facts do not decide the route question itself [RD-6].

rejected_claims.reason: Its unexcused-detour conclusion is accepted only in part: the 'no incident' limb is right on RD-4 [F14][RD-4], but the rider's own pre-segment authorisation F9 has to be weighed under RD-5 first, which is why the ruling turns on the scope of that consent rather than on the absence of an incident [F9][F3][RD-5].

Accepted that no RD-4(a) incident excuses the segment [F14][RD-4], but its blanket proposition that the rider's own authorisation cannot matter is rejected: F9 is a valid general consent before the segment, and it fails only because the extra kilometres fell outside its scope [F9][F1][F2][RD-5].

Accepted so far as it goes — F12's band window 12:03–12:27 does not cover the segment starting 12:27, and a band alone does not exempt under RD-4(b) [F12][F3][RD-4] — but it adds nothing, because the segment is resolved on the RD-5 scope reading.

Timing conceded (F8 at 12:24 precedes the segment start 12:27) [F8][F3], but it exempts nothing: timing fixes when the proposal was made, not that the driven route fell within the consent's scope [F3][RD-5].
Rejected: the absence of a measured stop in F3 only excludes RD-3; it does not extend a general authorisation to extra kilometres that failed its own speed standard [F3][F9][F1][F2][RD-5].

Rejected under RD-4(b): the PIE band 2 and Simei band 4 records are corroborative only and cannot exempt a segment standing alone, and the trace marks RD-4(a) ✗ with F14 recording no incident [F12][F13][F14][RD-4].

Partly rejected: the driver did flag the jam in-app before the segment [F8][F9], but F11 is a post-trip statement with no timestamp and states only that the rider said any faster way was fine — a claim about consent, not consent itself [F11][RD-5].

Rejected: the record does not show the PIE route would have been faster [F12][F14], but the duty is the shortest and most direct route, and F1/F2 show the trip was longer and slower than estimate, so absence of proof about the alternative route does not excuse the measured extra kilometres [F1][F2][RD-1].

Accepted only as to RD-6 — no account action attaches ([F16][F17][RD-6]) — but profile facts cannot decide the route question, so 302 trips and 0 disputes do not exempt the measured extra kilometres [F3][RD-6].
